dispositionKey.A: KEEP_AS_CERTIFIED — the span/category is legitimate as stored
dispositionKey.B: REPAIR_GEOMETRY — the category is correct, the span boundary is wrong
dispositionKey.C: RECLASSIFY — the semantic category is wrong
dispositionKey.D: SPLIT_SEMANTIC_UNIT — one stored unit holds two independently classifiable clauses
dispositionKey.E: WITHDRAW — the record does not belong as Q-authored semantic paint
dispositionKey.F: INTENTIONALLY_UNRESOLVED — the evidence does not establish one correct answer

rulesAppliedUniformly: A multi-line span is not a defect. Q writes one sentence over two lines constantly, and a complete semantic unit may hold line breaks, several clauses and a vocative. Where the span covers exactly one such unit it is KEPT.

A span lying ENTIRELY inside pasted or quoted material, covering exactly one complete unit of it, is KEPT. This queue is about boundary defects; whether quoted material may carry a certified category was settled elsewhere and is not re-litigated here. The prayer on #154, the Declaration on #3656, the Mueller scope order on #2943 and the three dictionary entries are all this case.
A span is REPAIRED when it swallows something that is not part of its unit: a certified record of another category, a label or cipher line, Q's signature, or a neighbouring independent sentence.

A span is WITHDRAWN when it is an extractor blob — three or more independent units, two or more of them already certified separately — so no single trim is correct. The sentences it leaves uncovered were never individually adjudicated and belong to the coverage census, not to this queue.

Where a repaired span still legitimately covers more than one sentence, the row survives the rebuild carrying an explicit reviewed disposition. That is the owner's standing instruction, not a failure to finish.
